Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-n4q5go2s/call-82e8e871968a4e47b34b57e0aaf4ff04/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command:
/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text()
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'Page {i}: {len(t)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
print('\\nFIRST PAGE\\n'+r.pages[0].extract_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
shutil.rmtree(Path('tmp/pdfs'))
print('Removed temporary PDF extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: The empirical contribution supports weak acceptance. MaskSub improves strong DeiT-III baselines across four model sizes by 0.6–0.7 percentage points at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs (Table 1). Selected three-seed results strengthen this evidence: ViT-B improves from 83.46 ± 0.04 to 84.08 ± 0.02 (Table A.12).

The core objective is technically coherent and practically simple: supervised learning on full images is combined with detached prediction targets for masked images, using shared parameters and no additional inference cost. Algorithm 1 and Appendix B provide useful implementation details, while Tables A.7–A.8 examine masking ratios and loss weights.

The paper meaningfully addresses additional training cost. ViT-B MaskSub reaches 84.1% in 25 GPU-days versus 83.7% in 26 GPU-days for longer baseline training (Table 7). Against CoSub, Table 8 reports higher accuracy with lower cost: 84.1% versus 83.9%, using 25.1 versus 35.3 GPU-days.

Evaluation extends substantially beyond ImageNet classification, including ResNet, Swin, pretrained-model fine-tuning, transfer learning, and robustness. The appendix reports gains on ADE20K and COCO, while ImageNet-A accuracy improves from 36.8% to 41.9% for ViT-B (Table A.4). This breadth supports the method's potential usefulness.
weaknesses: Conceptual originality is moderate: the method combines established masking and asymmetric self-distillation ideas, with its strongest contribution being their effective integration into modern recipes. Some comparisons overstate the distinction. Table 6 compares MaskSub with self-distillation results obtained under different training recipes; those results do not establish that earlier methods are incompatible with strong recipes, as asserted in Sections 2 and 4.3.

The explanation of automatic difficulty control is stronger than the evidence. In Equation (3), the masked-logit gradient is proportional to the disagreement between masked and full predictions, not to teacher correctness. A confidently incorrect teacher can still supply a strong erroneous target. Figure 3 supports an aggregate training trend, but does not establish the claim that masking effectively applies exclusively to successfully learned examples.

Some ablations leave attribution unclear. Table A.6 does not specify whether 'without KD loss' removes auxiliary supervision or replaces it with ground-truth supervision. Table A.7 also improves from the 77.4% baseline to 78.4% with zero masking, versus 79.2% with 50% masking. Thus, auxiliary training effects contribute materially alongside masking, and the specific benefit of the asymmetric distillation design is not fully isolated.

The benefits are less universal than the abstract suggests. Applying MaskSub during transfer fine-tuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.7% to 89.6% (Table 10). Section 4.2 explicitly states that CLIP's best-checkpoint accuracy is unchanged, despite improved final-epoch accuracy. Three-seed evidence supports selected central results, but uncertainty remains for smaller gains such as BEiTv2's 0.1-point improvements.

There are correctable reporting errors. Table 10 labels the ViT-S Cars improvement from 80.9% to 92.2% as +1.3 rather than +11.3 points. Section 4.4 claims approximately one-sixth of GradAug's MAE fine-tuning cost, whereas Table 9 reports 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU-days, approximately 37% of the total cost. These inaccuracies warrant correction but do not overturn the main empirical contribution.
